LOS ANGELES -- The No. 9 UCLA Bruins roster share a common destination, but the journeys that brought them to Westwood are anything but alike. When first-year head coach Bob Chesney arrived to campus, those individual journeys began to converge around a singular mission: resurrecting a program that had managed just three wins the previous season. Now, six games into a season few could have predicted, the Bruins are turning heads across college football — finishing the week as the last unbeaten team in the Big Ten conference. While standout performances have fueled UCLA on the field, the remarkable turnaround is about more than what happens between the lines. It is about the people and stories behind it. "It's really important to recognize individuals and let them be them," Chesney said Tuesday. "Everybody has a story to tell." Chesney began building UCLA’s culture in the preseason, encouraging players to share their motivations and aspirations as they navigate the pressures of college football. That emphasis on individual purpose and collective identity may be one of the driving forces behind the Bruins’ first 6-0 start since 2022. "To know you have a group that can keep this united, that you can trust and be open and vulnerable with is what we're ultimately trying to build," Chesney said. "When the light shines on somebody and they get a little more notice, those stories start to pop up," Chesney said. Perhaps the most interesting development surrounding UCLA’s start to the 2026 season is the emergence of quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who made his first start of the season in the Bruins’ 17-7 victory over Wisconsin on Saturday. The California native stepped into the starting role after senior quarterback Nico Iamaleava injured his knee during UCLA’s upset win over Oregon at Autzen Stadium in Week 6. For many teams, losing the starting quarterback could reveal hidden flaws and derail a promising season. Not UCLA. Not under Chesney. A next-man-up mentality, combined with a roster who plays with a chip on its shoulder, has fueled UCLA’s steady rise from unranked to top ten in the nation. The Bruins’ transformation has unfolded before the college football world, driven by a selfless group united by a singular goal — winning. item.title: Warriors’ Draymond Green hints at retirement heading into 15th NBA season
item.description: Warriors’ Draymond Green hints at retirement heading into 15th NBA season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After proving to be one of the best teams in NBA history throughout much of the past decade or so, the Golden State Warriors clearly aren't the same team that they once were. The Warriors still have a chance to be a good team because Stephen Curry and others are still elite, but the harsh reality is that guys aren't the same players they once were. This Warriors roster is also very different from what it was during other parts of what was considered a dynasty. As for guys like Draymond Green, he's late in his career. There haven't been any rumors suggesting that Green is going to retire just yet, but his recent comments make it seem like it's not as far away as some might think. “I would love to play basketball next year…if that’s not here, I’m not going to retire,” Green said , H/T ClutchPoints. “If I don’t (fit into the team's plans), great. But I’m extremely grateful for the journey that I’ve been on here.” “I don’t know how many years I have left in the NBA, let alone at this place. For me, it’s all about enjoying what’s in front of us.” Green signed a new deal with the Warriors during the offseason, an interesting move after trade rumors swirled around him. The 36-year-old Green will turn 37 in March of next year, so it's understandable if he decides to hang them up. There's a lot that's going to come into a situation like this, though it sounds like it's at least a possibility as of now. item.title: From 2013 NBA Finals to 2026 opening night, Sebastian De La Cruz returns to Spurs spotlight
item.description: Sebastian De La Cruz performs the national anthem before the San Antonio Spurs' season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday (Raul Trey Lopez) San Antonio native Sebastian De La Cruz returned to Frost Bank Center on Tuesday, performing the national anthem before the Spurs' season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Known as "El Charro de Oro," the 24-year-old singer wore a dark charro-inspired suit with gold embellishments and a colorful bow tie bearing the words "Crazy Hispanic Fans," a nod to the Spurs' fan base. De La Cruz has performed the national anthem for the Spurs at several milestone moments. He first gained national attention in 2013, when he sang before an NBA Finals game between the Spurs and Miami Heat. He was 11 at the time and became the target of racist comments online, prompting an outpouring of support from Spurs fans and the organization. Sebastian De La Cruz performs the national anthem before the San Antonio Spurs' season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday (Raul Trey Lopez) He returned to Frost Bank Center during the Spurs' 2026 playoff run, singing the anthem before Game 1 against the Portland Trail Blazers and again before Game 1 against the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Spurs entered this season after reaching the NBA Finals, where they lost to the New York Knicks. De La Cruz's latest performance continued his long-running connection with the team and its fans. item.title: NBA insider Shams Charania throws doubt at 76ers and Joel Embiid after recent comments
item.description: NBA insider Shams Charania throws doubt at 76ers and Joel Embiid after recent comments originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers will start the NBA season as one of the league's more interesting teams. There's reason to believe Philadelphia could be in a position to win a championship, though it remains uncertain how things will look on both sides of the ball because of some questions it has to answer. Mainly, those questions should come on the defensive side. As I've said before, if this 76ers offense isn't one of the best we've ever seen in the NBA, that will be a problem for head coach Nick Nurse. There's also the injury side of things, though there's reason to believe Philadelphia has guys who will be on the court every night outside of Joel Embiid and perhaps an older LeBron James. Embiid said earlier in the week that he understands that people have their concerns about sacrificing. However, the MVP said there is no reason to sacrifice anything, and guys can just play their game. That's the ideal outcome and a nice way to look at it, but it's probably unrealistic. Top NBA insider Shams Charania of ESPN pushed back on that notion, adding that someone or some players will have to sacrifice something. “Joel Embiid said the other day that there's no sacrifice… I have to say, there's going to be sacrifice. Someone or some player is going to have to sacrifice,” he said . The issue that could come up is that there is only one basketball on the court. That doesn't mean the 76ers' offense can't be great, but it's something to consider. I'm not as worried about that as some others seem to be, but I also think that suggesting nobody will have to sacrifice is wishful thinking and unrealistic. item.title: Russell Wilson suggests Jets should trade Garrett Wilson to Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs
item.description: Russell Wilson suggests Jets should trade Garrett Wilson to Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Amid the New York Jets ' struggles, some believe the organization could make a couple of trades at this year's trade deadline. At last year's trade deadline, the Jets moved on from some very good players, including Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams. At the time, it didn't seem like the Jets would move on from either of those guys, which makes it interesting to consider who could be available this time around. Among the options, trading a player like Garrett Wilson doesn't seem like it would make sense, but Russell Wilson believes there's a case for it, adding that if New York decides to move on from its star receiver, the Kansas City Chiefs are the most obvious suitor. “I'm just telling you, if I'm the Kansas City Chiefs, I got the All-Star running back in the backfield in Kenneth Walker, which we've never had before,” Wilson said , H/T Clutch Points. “And guess what that does? That play action opens up, right? What Mahomes does arguably better than anybody in the world is throw the ball down the field. “So, if I'm thinking about this, who would I go get? I'm gonna go get Garrett Wilson,” the ex-quarterback proclaimed. “If the Jets keep losing, I'm gonna go get Garrett Wilson from the New York Football Jets because I believe that Garrett Wilson, down the field, with his ability- he's a smart guy; he learns quickly- he'd be great in the Andy Reid style of offense… [The Chiefs] haven't had a receiver like him.” Trading Wilson would raise a lot of questions for the Jets, especially since he's been a guy who's said throughout his career that he wants to see things improve in New York and doesn't want to be traded. However, as guys like Gardner found out a season ago, this is a business at the end of the day. If the Jets believe moving on from Wilson and getting multiple draft picks in return is the better plan, that's exactly what will happen. item.title: Ravens rumors: Lamar Jackson expected to return to practice after 2-game absence
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Ravens rumors: Lamar Jackson expected to return to practice after 2-game absence appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It remains to be seen whether Lamar Jackson will finally be able to come back from a two-game absence and play in this coming Sunday’s game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium. But there appears to be more optimism about his status compared to last week . “Just as there was last week, there’s hope that Lamar Jackson is on the practice field tomorrow [Wednesday].” Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network shared on Tuesday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I would say more hope this week than last week. This was a chance, it was a multi-week injury. We are at two weeks. Lamar Jackson should, we’ll see, end up practicing this week and potentially play,” added the NFL insider. The two-time NFL Most Valuable Player sat out Baltimore’s Week 5 game against the Atlanta Falcons and the team’s Week 6 meeting with the Cleveland Browns . Tyler Huntley handled the quarterbacking chores in both games with different results, as the Ravens defeated the Falcons (30-23 via OT) and lost to the Browns (13-10). While the Ravens have confidence in Huntley, the team’s floor and ceiling are undeniably higher for Baltimore when it’s Jackson handling the rock. Over the four games he played so far in the 2026 season, the former Louisville Cardinals star quarterback has passed for 967 yards and six touchdowns against an interception on a 70.8 percent completion rate. He also has 144 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. After six weeks, the Ravens have a 4-2 record — tied with the Browns and Bengals for the best in the AFC North Division. item.title: Packers offensive coordinator reveals how excited he is to get Josh Jacobs back
item.description: Packers offensive coordinator reveals how excited he is to get Josh Jacobs back originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Reports indicate Green Bay Packers superstar running back Josh Jacobs will return to practice on Wednesday and could play against the Detroit Lions in Week 7. He served his time on the NFL's commissioner's exempt list, and Green Bay hoped it would eventually get him back. That's exactly what happened for a team looking to improve its run game, a promising sign for the Packers as they look to win a Super Bowl. Among the biggest problems for certain teams in the NFL this year, the Packers' run game was at the top of the list. As a contender, the Packers' run game wasn't going to put them in a position to win. After missing the first six weeks of the season, Jacobs will have to show he can be the player everyone expects him to be, and Green Bay coaches are understandably excited to have him back. “Josh [Jacobs] will definitely help, for sure,” said OC Adam Stenavich on the run game issues, H/T Heavy “He’s an excellent player, and he’ll provide some good spark for our offense. So, I’m excited about that. But we just all need to do a better job.” In the 2025 season, Jacobs played in 15 games, attempting 234 carries for 929 yards. He averaged 4.0 yards per carry, including 13 touchdowns. In 2024, he was even better, rushing for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns. item.title: Unioto's Kinzli Batson, Adena's Kimmy Dalton named SVC POYs
item.description: CHILLICOTHE — Through every twist and turn on this season's journey, Unioto's Kinzli Batson has been there to lead her teammates to their eventual destination. On Wednesday morning, she was rewarded for her steady hand. Batson was named the Scioto Valley Conference Player of the Year, becoming the first Sherman to earn that honor since 2017. The junior posted 55 kills, 43 aces, 37 blocks, 189 digs and 749 assists — including the 1,000th of her career — to lead Unioto to a 12-2 record in league play. Adena's Kimmy Dalton also earned individual honors, being named the SVC's Defensive Player of the Year for the third consecutive season. In 76 sets, Dalton has collected 469 digs while handling 416 serve receptions. She enters postseason play with a career total of 1,520 digs. item.title: ‘Ragdolled’ – NBA fans can’t believe 6’3″ De’Aaron Fox tossed 7’1″ Chet Holmgren in Thunder vs. Spurs
item.description: Credit: Christian Petersen/Getty Images The San Antonio Spurs and OKC Thunder got into a scuffle during their 2026-27 NBA season opener against each other. The Spurs are hoping to prove that they didn’t need the Thunder to be wrecked with injuries to beat them in the Conference Finals in their full-strength matchup against OKC on opening night. Regardless of the outcome, everyone can see that this young Western Conference rivalry is bound to grow from strength to strength after a heated altercation between De’Aaron Fox and Chet Holmgren at the start of the second quarter. De’Aaron Fox tossing Chet Holmgren during scuffle has left NBA fans stunned During an attempted pass to the 7’1″ Holmgren, the 6’3″ guard Fox decided the most effective way of stopping the mismatch would be to pull Holmgren down, but he wound up tossing the Thunder big man to the ground with visible force. While Fox did deserve the Flagrant 1 foul he received for that aggressive foul, the way Holmgren went flying is the main takeaway from most fans who saw the interaction. “Chet just got ragdolled by a 6’3″ PG,” said one bemused fan . “The way Chet acts, you’d never believe he’s a 7-footer,” lamented a fan . “How you gonna let a guard throw you like that, Chet?” questioned a stunned fan . “Chet is still soft as ever, I see,” said one fan after the interaction . “How does Chet even get tossed like that by De’Aaron Fox?” questioned another fan . Fox is listed as a 6’3″ point guard who weighs 185 pounds, compared to Holmgren, who is a 7’1″ power forward/center who weighs 208 pounds. Even if Holmgren is not as heavy as most of his counterparts at his size and position, he still outweighs Fox by over 10 pounds while being substantially taller. The optics of Holmgren being shoved to the ground that easily by a guard are just very ugly. Thankfully, Holmgren and the Thunder can potentially move on from this situation with a win, as they are currently leading the Spurs 65-44 at halftime. Holmgren has eight points and two blocks, while Fox has four points, four rebounds and two assists. item.title: One team stands out more than others in potential Eagles’ Saquon Barkley
item.description: One team stands out more than others in potential Eagles’ Saquon Barkley originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . If the Philadelphia Eagles decide to move on from players, a couple of NFL teams will find it hard not to go after them. At the top of that list would be the Seattle Seahawks and Houston Texans , two teams that have a chance to figure some things out over the next couple of months. There's reason to believe the Texans and Seahawks are both playoff-caliber teams, despite not having the seasons they hoped for entering the season. The Texans are a bit more interesting considering the Seahawks won a Super Bowl a year ago, but regardless, the Eagles should find themselves in a position to be able to trade Barkley to a contending team similar to those two that have struggled offensively, which should give them a chance to improve their draft assets over the next couple of seasons. “I could see a few contenders doing it. The Seahawks came to mind, as did the Packers and the Vikings . But I love the idea of GM Nick Caserio, fresh off the Marvin Harrison Jr. deal, doubling down on the offense and adding Barkley to a backfield that he has yet to solve in Houston,” Ben Solak wrote . “The Texans are once again on pace to have a bottom-5 rushing attack, but Barkley has the talent behind the line of scrimmage to help cover for a shaky interior offensive line group. By forcing opposing defenses to play more heavy boxes by formation and by the presence of Barkley, the 2-4 Texans could pull further defensive attention away from receiver Nico Collins and field an offense really worthy of a comeback run into the playoffs.” For Philadelphia, the bigger focus is what it can get in return in a potential trade package. There's a lot to like about what the Eagles could get back, but there's also the argument that moving him now won't get them the same trade package they would have a few seasons ago. Barkley is still among the better running backs in the NFL, but he'll be 30 soon, and historically, running backs start to struggle at that age. item.description: © Christine Tannous/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Dan Hurley blows a kiss to heckling Michigan State fans during exhibition appeared first on ClutchPoints . During his tenure as head coach of the UConn Huskies, Dan Hurley has certainly embraced the troll persona he’s seemingly acquired from opposing teams’ fans. In UConn’s case, the Huskies are looking to get back to the national championship game following a disappointing defeat last season at the hands of the Michigan Wolverines. item.title: Lakers get major Bronny James update before season opener vs. Warriors
item.description: Lakers get major Bronny James update before season opener vs. Warriors originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers are heading into their first season without LeBron James in almost a decade, so things will be different for the organization. Still, the team will have his son, Bronny James, on the roster for his third season as an NBA guard. The two made NBA history together but will now be on separate teams. For the younger James, it is all about making a name for himself now that his dad is in Philadelphia. “You guys know me as Bronny. My real name is LeBron. I've been doing this for however long, so I think it's a motivating factor for me just getting up every day and trying to prove myself as Bronny instead of LeBron,” he said. The Lakers are opening the season on Wednesday against the Golden State Warriors , officially ushering in a new era. James is hoping to carve out a role for himself. However, on Monday, he didn’t practice due to an illness. “Am told that Bronny James is genuinely ill and was home sick from practice,” The Athletic’s Dan Woike wrote. With this development, James’ status for Wednesday’s opener was unclear, as the severity of his illness was not immediately known. The Lakers needed James in the first round of the playoffs last season when they were thin on available players. Both sides are hoping he will develop as the season progresses so he can earn key minutes. James was back at practice Tuesday and is good to go for Wednesday. “Bronny James is back at practice after being excused from yesterday's session because of an illness,” California Post’s Khobi Price wrote. It will be intriguing to see how many minutes James plays in his third season and whether he can contribute in a bigger way. His future with the Lakers could depend on how he performs this season, making it an important year for him to prove himself. The Lakers will be led by Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, but the question is where James fits into the rotation. With James back from his illness, Wednesday’s opener could offer an early glimpse into the Lakers’ plans for him. item.title: Adam Schefter challenges claims of Eagles mishandling Jalen Hurts’ medical situation
item.description: ESPN’s NFL insider Adam Schefter has challenged claims that the Philadelphia Eagles mishandled Jalen Hurts ’ medical situation. The quarterback is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs. The situation has raised questions about why Hurts played against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London after doctors identified a blood clot in his calf. However, Schefter believes more information is needed before blaming Philadelphia. Speaking to 97.5 The Fanatic hosts Jon Marks and Andrew Salciunas, Schefter questioned what punishment the Eagles could face. “What’s the penalty?” Schefter asked. “What is the league penalizing them for?” MORE: Former Eagles receiver sends prayers to Jalen Hurts after health scare Marks suggested the NFL Players Association could investigate whether Philadelphia allowed Hurts to play despite knowing about the blood clot. He also questioned whether the team had misrepresented the condition on its injury report. Schefter acknowledged the concern but resisted drawing conclusions before the facts were established. “They did list him as a calf,” Schefter said. “Do you list him in that particular case? Because teams are fudging injury reports all the time… have we seen teams list players on the report with a blood clot? And are they violating the rules by saying it’s a calf? I don’t know.” Adam Schefter separates medical concerns from potential rule violations Tottenham, ENG; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Schefter emphasized that the Eagles could face consequences if investigators found they manipulated the injury report. However, he questioned whether listing a calf injury violated league rules when the underlying diagnosis involved a clot. “If they did something wrong, the league will come down on them,” Schefter said. “I don’t know if I see something wrong. “I know what we all think. item.title: Eagles star strangely says Tanner McKee could end up being like Tom Brady
item.description: Eagles star strangely says Tanner McKee could end up being like Tom Brady originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles need some kind of boost from anyone on the roster right now, and Tanner McKee would be the biggest of them all. McKee has done a very good job of coming in and doing what's needed when called upon, but now, as a full-time starter for the remainder of the season, unless the Eagles decide to make a trade, things will be more difficult than ever before. McKee doesn't seem like a guy who is going to come in and instantly be a perfect fit for Philadelphia, but he can definitely be serviceable. History says he's not elite by any means, but don't say that to one Philadelphia star. He believes that he has a chance to follow the career arc that Tom Brady did. “I love Tanner,” said Zack Baun, H/T SB Nation . “I love that guy so much. I told someone that it’s just seeming like he’s got some sort of Tom Brady career arc to him, because he’s totally capable, he’s tall, he knows where to go with the ball, he gets it out on time and he’s got a lot of confidence in these receivers.” Obviously, Baun will stick up for his guy, and there's nothing wrong with that. However, suggesting he can be anything like Brady seems a bit ridiculous. At the same time, some of what Baun is saying isn't really unfair, given that he trusts his receivers and hopes to figure some things out. At the end of the day, the Eagles need guys to step up, and McKee is the primary candidate. Hopefully, he can be even a shell of Brady in terms of winning games at a high level, and Philadelphia can go on a nice stretch to end the season. item.title: Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns unlikely to be traded, despite contract problems
item.description: Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns unlikely to be traded, despite contract problems originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks are in a strong position to go back-to-back this season if things go according to plan, though the organization still has a few things to consider. For one, the Knicks won't have an easy time winning it all, even if they stay healthy all season. They found out last year just how difficult it is to win a championship, even during that historic run. As for other problems, the Knicks keep making questionable decisions with star center Karl-Anthony Towns. Towns, undoubtedly one of the better players in the NBA, finds himself in a strange contract situation. Reports indicate he's willing to take less than the max, but it's still unclear what's holding things up. Because of that, some have recently suggested he could be traded. “Look, the Knicks have set themselves up to be fixtures on the NBA trade rumor market this season. Trading away Towns would be terribly unwise for the Knicks, but not settling on an extension for Towns as he heads toward free agency was unwise, too. “So the fact that the Knicks have not done the second thing leads to an assumption that they’re at least somewhat open to do the first thing. Is there an offer that would get the Knicks to the table? Probably not. But it will be endlessly discussed,” Sean Deveney wrote . Moving on from Towns really doesn't make a whole lot of sense for the Knicks as they search to go back-to-back. Teams have certainly done worse things in the past, but the Knicks have the money, a team that just won a championship, and one of the best players in the world next to their superstar Jalen Brunson. Letting that happen again would be a very questionable decision. item.title: The Red Sox Have Clear Path to Play Franklin Arias, Trevor Story, and Curtis Mead
item.description: The Red Sox Have Clear Path to Play Franklin Arias, Trevor Story, and Curtis Mead originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Some Boston Red Sox fans are rightfully worried the team won't be able to keep Franklin Arias, Trevor Story, and Curtis Mead on the roster next season. While the Red Sox will certainly have decisions to make this offseason, there are many reasons to believe things can be just fine with those three guys around. The Red Sox will likely have to get creative, but Boston's insider for The Athletic recently proposed one possibility. One option would be to play Arias or Story at second or shortstop, Mead at third base, or even use one of them as a designated hitter. “One scenario could entail shifting Mead to designated hitter with Arias and Story at either second or short. Mead broke out at the plate last season for the Washington Nationals with 17 homers and 17 doubles in 84 games. “His season ended in late July in his first game following a trade to the Red Sox when a pitch hit and broke his wrist. Still, the Red Sox traded for him for his offensive potential, and a DH role for next season may be how they make the roster work. He could then slide back to second in 2028 with Arias at short,” Jen McCaffrey wrote . Among the designated hitter options, it feels like Mead or Story would be that guy. The reason is that bringing up Arias at just 21, as he turns 21 on Nov. 19, wouldn't be the wisest decision for the young man. If the Red Sox are going to call him up, he needs to play every single day in the field. item.title: NFLPA calls for “full investigation” into Jalen Hurts situation
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the National Anthem before the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier on Tuesday, the NFL concluded that Jalen Hurts being cleared to play with a superficial blood clot was “ handled appropriately .” On Tuesday evening, the NFL Players Association pushed back on that assertion with an official statement: The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward. The NFLPA isn’t necessarily casting doubt on the NFL’s stance. They’re calling for more transparency, which they’re well within their rights to do. It’s not their function to merely take the league at their word. If everything was truly above board in how the Eagles handled Hurts’ medical situation, a “full investigation” into the matter should reveal as much. The team and the league should be fully cooperative with the NFLPA if they have nothing to hide. It’ll be interesting to see what comes of this request.

item.description: Rams’ Matthew Stafford has chance to make brutal NFL history in game against Raiders originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's been a very strange start to the 2026-27 NFL season for the Los Angeles Rams , who are currently sitting in fourth place in the NFC West despite expectations that they'd be the best team in the NFL to start the year. The Rams haven't been able to get much going on either side of the football, though the offense has certainly been the bigger problem. After winning the MVP award last season, quarterback Matthew Stafford hasn't exactly played great football. Not that everything is Stafford's fault on offense, but he's thrown just 11 touchdowns and six interceptions in the first six weeks of the season. To make matters worse, Stafford could reach some unfortunate NFL history over the next few weeks if the Rams keep playing this way. “Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford lost his fourth start of the season on Sunday. When he loses his fifth, he’ll reach a career milestone he’d prefer not to have,” Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio wrote , H/T PFT. “Stafford has a career record of 122-122-1 as a starting quarterback. Those 122 losses are the second-most in NFL history, behind only Vinny Testaverde, who went 90-123-1. With another loss, Stafford will tie Testaverde for the most ever, and with two more losses, Stafford has the record all to himself.” The Rams and Stafford have much more to worry about than him taking over for the most starts in NFL history as a quarterback and still losing, but it does show that the start of his career certainly wasn't kind to him with the Detroit Lions . Things have obviously improved in Los Angeles, winning a Super Bowl back in 2022. For now, however, the focus is on winning games in 2026, and the Rams haven't done that. item.description: Why NFLPA is demanding investigation into Eagles' handling of Jalen Hurts blood clot situation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL seemingly cleared the Eagles of any rule violations in their handling of Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis, with The Athletic reporting Tuesday that the league found no reason for discipline for Philadelphia's handling of the injury report or the decision to play Hurts after he was found to have a superficial blood clot in his calf. Both NFL chief medical officer Alan Sills and executive vice president Jeff Miller defended the Eagles, with Sills calling reports that Hurts stayed awake for 36 hours so he could play against the Jaguars "nonsense." While that report was refuted — Hurts did play against the Jaguars but reportedly slept before the game after a hospital visit kept him awake — the NFL Players Association is still looking for answers. Here's a look at how the NFLPA is turning up the heat on the NFL and the Eagles. MORE: Eagles' best QB options in winnable NFC East NFLPA demands investigation into Jalen Hurts situation The NFL Players Association released a statement Tuesday night bemoaning the NFL's lack of investigation into the Eagles' handling of Hurts' blood clot situation. "Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred," the NFLPA said. "Determining the facts is essential to to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward." https://t.co/wZyVLPcXvD — NFLPA (@NFLPA) October 21, 2026 The NFL confirmed earlier Tuesday that it wouldn't discipline the Eagles for both the decision to play Hurts after a superficial blood clot was found in his calf or for not listing Hurts with an game designation on the injury report before the London game against the Jaguars. The Eagles received backlash after a report indicated Hurts had to stay awake for 36 hours just to play in the game, but reports have subsequently refuted that suggestion, instead claiming Hurts slept before the game after a hospital visit for tests on his calf kept him awake longer than his teammates. NFL EVP Jeff Miller called the original reporting "uninformed as he and chief medical officer Alan Sills pushed back on the idea Hurts was mistreated. Hurts was ruled out for the season on Monday after multiple blood clots were found in his lungs; he is expected to be treated with blood thinners for three months. item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - JULY 05: Babies crawl before a game between the Savannah Bananas and The Firefighters at Fenway Park on July 05, 2025 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images Taylor Smith knows numbers — his resume includes analytics work with the data-centric Tampa Bay Rays. But when fans look at Smith, only one number pops up first in their minds and it relates neither to launch angles nor spin rate. Smith is defined by the number 31, as he embarks on his new role as the youngest in the industry. By a fair bit. item.title: Dave Portnoy calls out Vikings over handling of J.J. McCarthy
item.description: Dave Portnoy calls out Vikings over handling of J.J. McCarthy originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Minnesota Vikings first-round pick J.J. McCarthy got his first action with the New York Giants as a legitimate option this past Sunday in Week 6 against the New Orleans Saints , attempting 21 passes and completing 11. McCarthy certainly didn't have the best stat line, completing just 52.4% of his passes, but he also threw for 243 yards and a touchdown. He looked to be a serviceable option for the Giants, and at 23 years old, there's reason to believe he can eventually be just that. In regard to how others felt, some are taking it a step further. That includes Dave Portnoy, the Barstool founder, owner, and University of Michigan fan. Portnoy has loved McCarthy ever since he helped Michigan win a national title, rightfully so, but believes that he didn't get a fair shake in Minnesota. In regards to that comment alone, it's not unfair to say that Portnoy has a point. “I never thought he got a fair shake in Minnesota. He never got a fair shake. He got hurt right away and then never got back in the flow. I’ve always been a JJ fan. I saw what he did every single game at Michigan. I said when the Giants got him, they got a winner,” Portnoy said , H/T Heavy. There are a couple of ways to look at what Portnoy is saying, but the reality is that McCarthy didn't get a fair chance in terms of games played. He appeared in only 10 games for the Vikings and dealt with multiple injuries during his time with the organization. Given the talent he showed at Michigan, it's not a crazy idea to suggest he could be a good player one day. Perhaps he's not the perfect answer for what the Giants are looking to do this season, and there are obviously questions about whether he'll play next year with Jaxson Dart returning, but if he can get his career back on track, there's reason to believe he can be a decent player one day. The comedian was suggesting that the 22-year-old belongs in junior college basketball rather than the NBA. Morgan was in a feisty mood throughout the segment, making it clear he had no plans to hold back. The Knicks received their rings and raised their championship banner before opening the season against the Philadelphia 76ers, who signed LeBron James this summer. The four-time NBA champion was making his regular-season debut with Philadelphia at MSG, putting his son squarely in the conversation. item.title: Raiders Owner Mark Davis Shares Honest Thoughts About Fernando Mendoza
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza. Getty When last season ended and the Las Vegas Raiders got the No. 1 pick, it was expected that Fernando Mendoza would be the team’s starting quarterback this season. However, they signed Kirk Cousins before the draft, but it wasn’t clear what the plan was for him. It quickly became evident that new head coach Klint Kubiak preferred to bring Mendoza along slowly. He previously worked with Cousins on the Minnesota Vikings, so he knew he could trust the quarterback. That decision has actually paid off, as Cousins is currently tied for the NFL lead with 14 touchdown passes. Mendoza did get one chance to play against the New England Patriots in a blowout loss, but there hasn’t been much talk of him supplanting Cousins quite yet. Raiders owner Mark Davis hasn’t seen the team draft a quarterback in the first round until this year. There’s no doubt he’d love to see the future face of his franchise play, but Davis doesn’t like to meddle in football affairs. From what he’s seen, he’s very happy with Mendoza so far. “I love his work ethic,” Davis told The New York Post . “I love that he’s like a sponge in terms of learning.” Davis Thinks Mendoza Will Be Great The Raiders are fortunate that Cousins has played well, as it has helped quiet any conversation about benching him for Mendoza. However, Cousins is 38 and not going to be the long-term starter. The future of the Raiders hinges on how good Mendoza ends up being. Davis has been impressed with the young quarterback’s desire to be an all-time great. “He wants to be the greatest. He enjoys the game, he’s competitive,” Davis said. “Everything you think of, he’s got.” Davis is remaining confident in the No. 1 pick. “If he can play football, he’s going to be great,” Davis said. Will Mendoza Start This Season? The Raiders are starting to get in a bind. They are in the midst of a three-game losing streak and are 3-3. The three losses aren’t on Cousins, who has mostly played at a high level. It’ll be difficult to bench him if he’s playing well. At the same time, if the playoffs are out of reach, it could make more sense to eventually give Mendoza some more reps. The problem with that is once they make the decision to start the rookie, they can’t go back. That’s why the Raiders are remaining patient right now. The team can’t run the ball right now, which is a problem for a rookie quarterback. Mendoza had an excellent run game to rely on at Indiana. The Raiders also have major question marks along the offensive line and at wide receiver. There’s plenty of merit to the idea of just having him redshity this season. Next year, they can address the issues on the offensive line and in the wide receiver room. By then, they have the run game figured out as well. Now, if the Raiders get completely knocked out of the playoff race, it might not hurt to give him a chance, but it’s too early in the season to make that call. item.title: 76ers' LeBron James accuses NBA refs of giving Knicks a championship whistle in season opener
item.description: 76ers' LeBron James accuses NBA refs of giving Knicks a championship whistle in season opener originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers have put together quite the roster to make a serious run at a championship. For that reason, many people have their eyes on the team to see how things play out this season. The 76ers have a deep starting five that could give opposing teams fits. However, people like Jeff Teague don't believe they have what it takes to compete for a championship. “Everybody got a lot of high hopes for the Sixers, I'm not a fan. I don't think they going to be that good. I got them 4th seed in the East… It's too much sacrifice, who's going to sacrifice all that? The first time they go on a 4 game losing streak and they start saying something to Bron. Well you know Bron is old, some sh*t going to happen," Teague said. On Tuesday, the 76ers opened their season with a win over the New York Knicks . LeBron James felt good about how his team performed. “I feel a lot better. Still getting my rhythm. Obviously, you know, just a little bit over two weeks with the new squad. I like the way we play. I think we played exceptionally well, especially defensively. We didnt shoot the ball well, but we have capable shooters. We know that. It’s about winning. Just trying to make plays to win,” James said. During the game, James was caught talking trash to a fan, and the exchange seemed to get him going. The four-time NBA champion was also caught on a hot mic commenting on the officiating, suggesting the Knicks were already receiving a championship whistle. “They win one chip they get a championship whistle,” James said. Philadelphia did commit more fouls than New York, but the difference was only one. Still, James appeared to believe the Knicks were already getting some favorable calls, and his comments were caught on a hot mic. The 76ers spoiled the Knicks' ring ceremony by earning the victory. Philadelphia will now play in front of its home crowd on Thursday, where James could have another opportunity to make his presence felt. item.description: CLEMSON, SC - OCTOBER 17: Clemson players run down the hill to enter the stadium during a college football game between the Charleston Southern Buccaneers and the Clemson Tigers on October 17, 2026 at Clemson Memorial Stadium in Clemson, S.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Virginia Tech Hokies (5-2, 2-2) snapped a two-game losing streak on Saturday, defeating the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 34-24. Technically, the Hokies are only two plays away from being 7-0. That may sound hopeful, optimistic, or something else, but it’s also true. Next up for the Hokies is a trip to Clemson. And while these Tigers aren’t the same Clemson teams from 2012-2022, they’re still the team most ACC programs measure themselves against. A win in Death Valley would be a huge statement win for James Franklin in his first year as Virginia Tech’s head coach. Clemson enters next week’s game with a 4-2 record, including a 2-1 mark in ACC play. Here are the teams that Clemson has beaten: Georgia Southern, North Carolina, California and Charleston Southern. item.title: Blake Griffin points out Clippers refusal to honor ‘Lob City’ era teams
item.description: Blake Griffin reveals the Clippers have not reached out to honor "Lob City" era teams. One of the greatest eras of Clippers basketball took place during the 2010’s when “Lob City” was in full effect . Blake Griffin, who was the face of the Clippers during this era, told Front Office Sports that the organization hasn’t done anything to honor those past teams. Blake Griffin says the Clippers have never reached out to the “Lob City” group, which made six straight playoff trips with him and Chris Paul. "I don’t think we’ve ever been asked to come back or do anything or honor that team.” Full story: https://t.co/oo1raKlsF6 pic.twitter.com/5YTXWqzq7n — Front Office Sports (@FOS) October 20, 2026 Blake Griffin reveals the Clippers have yet to honor past “Lob City” era teams. Anthony J. Causi “I don’t think we’ve ever been asked to come back or do anything to honor that team,” Griffin said. Between 1997-2011, the Clippers were perennial outcasts when it came down to making the playoffs. The team had only one playoff appearance during this 14-year period in 2006, when they were eliminated in the second round by the Phoenix Suns. Griffin played for the team between 2009-2018 he and Chris Paul helped change the identity of the team entirely. During the “Lob City” era, the Clippers made the playoffs six straight years and made it out of the first round three times, in 2012, 2014, and 2015. “You look back and have a sense of pride because of what the Clippers were before, and it was often a punchline,” Griffin said. “I think that we feel pride in that we sort of got that franchise to a place where it was like, ‘Oh no, you’re expected to make the playoffs. You’re expected to go further.” Blake Girffin guarding Knicks’ Kristaps Porzingis as a member of the Clippers during an NBA game in 2017. Anthony Causi While the Clippers were starting to be taken seriously in the NBA spotlight, one of Griffin’s iconic moments for the organization happened during the 2010-2011 season. Not only was Griffin the NBA’s Dunk Contest champion that season , he also became the fifth member of the organization, and first since they’ve been in Los Angeles, to win the Rookie of the Year award when he averaged 22.5 points, 12.1 rebounds, 0.8 steals, and 0.5 blocks per game. Aside from Griffin being disappointed in the organization not willing to recognize their past teams, Griffin spoke about the team’s controversial decision to release Paul in the middle of the year , during his final NBA season. item.title: Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard drops poignant video ahead of season opener
item.description: Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard drops poignant video ahead of season opener appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kawhi Leonard was going to come home, one way or another, this past offseason. His hometown may be in LA, and he may have played with the Los Angeles Clippers for seven seasons, but his basketball home will always be north of the border — with the Toronto Raptors welcoming their prodigal son back with open arms. Leonard, in a poignant video he posted on his official X account ahead of the Raptors’ season-opening clash against the Chicago Bulls, shared just how much the year he spent with the team means to him , and how he’s raring to go on a similarly magical run with this new-look squad seven seasons after he left in free agency. “One thing I’ve learned about time: people move on. Things change. And even the greatest moments become memories. But some things, some things stay with you. What we shared here, that’s forever,” Leonard said. “They say the second time isn’t as good as the first, but we’ll see.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It wasn’t luck the first time. And I still know what it takes.” As I Return. pic.twitter.com/yMv1iqMt30 — Kawhi Leonard (@Way2Whi) October 20, 2026 The Raptors certainly believe that Leonard could help this young team they have get over the hump in a loaded Eastern Conference. They traded away Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, an unprotected pick swap, and two second-round picks to the Clippers to re-acquire the services of the 2019 NBA Finals MVP. It’s a testament to how beloved Leonard is among Raptors fans for his playoff heroics that they still welcomed him back even though he chose the glitz and glamour of LA over staying in Toronto seven years ago. Moreover, he didn’t exactly cover himself in glory in the way his Clippers tenure ended — in a cap circumvention controversy that had him fined $700,000 for his role in that scandal. But Leonard did prove to be the missing piece for the Raptors after years of coming up short in the playoffs. Will Toronto catch lighting in a bottle twice? The 35-year-old star certainly is confident that they have what it takes to do so.

item.title: ‘Seen everything’ – Reggie Miller shocked after seeing what Spike Lee did during LeBron James’ Knicks fan interaction
item.description: Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images NBA legend Reggie Miller was stunned to see New York Knicks superfan Spike Lee talk to LeBron James. LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers have started the 2026-27 NBA season on a positive note with a stunning 106-100 win at Madison Square Garden. One of the most talked-about moments from the game was James engaging in a back-and-forth battle with a courtside Knicks fan. James faced the wrath of Knicks fans the entire game due to snubbing the defending champions in the offseason. But as for James’ clapback at the fan, an unexpected Knicks supporter became the mediator between them. Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images Reggie Miller was shocked to see Spike Lee trying to diffuse LeBron James’ verbal battle with a fan Spike Lee is considered one of the biggest Knicks fans of all time as the popular filmmaker has supported the team for decades. During which, Lee has built a reputation of being a vocal fan who supports Knicks supporter no matter what. However, for a change, Lee decided to be the calm voice and tried to diffuse the situation between James and a Knicks fan. This intervention from Lee had NBA legend Reggie Miller stunned as he shared his reaction during the in-game broadcast. “Guess who’s playing peacemaker [between LeBron and fan]? Spike Lee. He’s over here playing peacemaker. Wow, I’ve seen everything,” Miller said during the game. Miller was equally shocked at Lee greeting him before the game, instead of spewing any insults towards the Indiana Pacers icon. Well, it seems the Knicks winning the NBA Championship after 53 years has turned Lee soft. It will be interesting to see how long this change lasts, as the Knicks have already started the season with a defeat against the 76ers. Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
